name: Prompt to install an app from an untrusted, non-store source
description: The recipient is prompted to install an app or APK delivered through a message, link or social post rather than an official store. NARROWED (2026-08-28): the iOS configuration-profile mechanism is excluded — CERT-In supports the generic untrusted-install concept only.

source_references.document_ref: iOS/Apple malicious side-loading advisory (original PDF unavailable)

manual_retrieval.notes: Original iOS advisory (SRC-025) still unavailable. CERT-In supports 'use trusted/authorised app stores; avoid apps from messages/social links'. Does NOT support the iOS configuration-profile mechanism — that clause is narrowed out and stays unsupported.

source_references.quote: Since our Play Protect pilot rolled out in October 2024 in India, it has blocked nearly 6 crore (60 million) attempts to install high-risk apps

explanation.plain: You were sent a link to install an app directly, outside the official app store. Apps delivered this way are a common way to plant malware. Install apps only from the official store, never from a link in a message.
explanation.technical: An untrusted/non-store install prompt (device-action) with a link/impersonation/unsolicited vector. CERT-In supports the trusted-store guidance; Google evidences the scale of blocked high-risk installs.
verification_steps: Install apps only from the official app store; delete APKs sent by message.
Check the developer name in the store before installing.
explanation.why_confidence_limited: Narrowed to the generic untrusted-install concept: the iOS configuration-profile mechanism has no verified basis and is excluded. Evidence is an official replacement (CERT-In) plus industry prevalence (Google); capped at MEDIUM. Held at PEER_REVIEW.

provenance.notes: PARTIAL at Phase 1 (SRC-025 unreachable; SRC-010 prevalence only). Reconciled to CERT-In replacement support (MR-EVID-011) under DEC-006 / ADR-0015; iOS configuration-profile clause narrowed out and left as an open gap.
